daily.title: Timely Section 148A(b) Notice Cannot Save Time-Barred Reassessment Under Section 148: ITAT
daily.summary: Hyderabad ITAT condones 763-day appeal delay and quashes reassessment as Section 148 notice was issued beyond the six-year limitation period. The Hyderabad ITAT held that issuing a show-cause notice under Section 148A(b) within six years from the end of the relevant assessment year did not preserve the Assessing Officer’s jurisdiction to issue a notice under Section 148 after that period expired. The first proviso to Section 149(1) preserved the limitation applicable under the earlier reassessment regime. The exclusions and extensions under the fifth and sixth provisos could not enlarge that outer limit.

daily.title: ITAT Quashes Time-Barred Reassessment Beyond Ten Years, Deletes ₹16.91 Crore Addition
daily.summary: Delhi ITAT quashes reassessment for AY 2012-13 under Section 149 limitation, resulting in deletion of ₹16.91 crore addition under Section 68. The Delhi ITAT held that the first proviso to Section 149(1) preserves the limitation applicable under the pre-2021 reassessment and search assessment provisions. Where the relevant assessment year was already beyond the permissible period under the earlier law, a subsequent notice under Section 148 could not revive it. The Tribunal accordingly upheld the quashing of the reassessment for AY 2012–13 , which had resulted in an addition of ₹16.91 crore under Section 68 .
